question: How is Diginex positioned against larger ESG software competitors like Workiva or Enablon?

beats.line: Diginex sits in a different market position from Workiva.
beats.headline: DIFFERENT POSITION
events: A tall paper building drops onto the ground and settles, opening cold.
A small cream paper chip slides in and stops at its base.
A paper hand taps the chip flat beside the building.
beats.delivery: [presenting to camera] Diginex sits in a different market position from Workiva.

beats.line: Workiva is a seven billion dollar market cap public company.
beats.headline: $7B+
events: The tall paper building holds its place as a stack of paper documents enters from the edge.
The documents pile higher against the building's side.
A black chip slaps in beside the pile and holds.
beats.delivery: Workiva is a seven billion dollar market cap public company.

beats.line: Diginex, at thirty-four million market cap, is a micro-cap challenger.
beats.headline: $34M
events: The building and document stack stay put as a tiny paper chip enters low on the ground.
The chip creeps toward the building's base and stops, dwarfed.
A large black chip slaps in over the tiny one, printing the figure.
beats.delivery: [excited] Diginex, at thirty-four million market cap, is a micro-cap challenger.

beats.line: Diginex plays horizontal platform consolidation, not vertical depth.
beats.headline: HORIZONTAL PLATFORM
events: The violet chips flip away as the ground turns cyan and a wide paper sheet unrolls flat.
A stencilled arrow sweeps sideways across the sheet.
A black chip lands at the arrow's end.
beats.delivery: Diginex plays horizontal platform consolidation, not vertical depth.

beats.line: One platform spans carbon, supply chain, and customer data.
beats.headline: 3 MODULES
events: The wide paper sheet stays flat as three hole-punched tags drop in along it.
A paper hand slides each tag into its slot on the sheet.
The last tag clicks into place and a chip lands beside it.
beats.delivery: [fast-paced] One platform spans carbon, supply chain, and customer data.

beats.line: The bet is enterprises prefer one vendor to point solutions.
beats.headline: SINGLE VENDOR
events: The sheet and tags hold as a rubber stamp swings in from above.
A paper hand presses the stamp down across all three tags at once.
The stamp lifts, leaving one mark, and a chip slaps in.
beats.delivery: The bet is enterprises prefer one vendor to point solutions.

beats.line: This only works if cross-sell actually happens across modules.
beats.headline: IF CROSS-SELL
events: The cyan chips slide off the top edge as a grid of paper squares lands on magenta ground.
String and pins stretch between squares, then one line goes slack.
A black chip drops onto the empty square.
beats.delivery: This only works if cross-sell actually happens across modules.

beats.line: Four acquisitions across multiple geographies is complex.
beats.headline: 4 ACQUISITIONS
events: The paper grid holds as four torn strips fall in from the edge.
A paper hand tries to tape the strips together across the grid.
One strip curls loose as a black chip lands over it.
beats.delivery: Four acquisitions across multiple geographies is complex.

beats.line: Diginex has an eighteen to twenty-four month window to prove traction.
beats.headline: 18–24 MONTHS
events: The magenta strips are covered as the ground returns to violet and the tall paper building reappears.
A paper calendar strip unrolls past the building and stops.
A paper hand pins the strip's far end and a chip lands.
beats.delivery: Diginex has an eighteen to twenty-four month window to prove traction.

beats.line: Micro-cap valuation prices in execution uncertainty, and upside is asymmetric.
beats.headline: ASYMMETRIC UPSIDE
events: The tall paper building stands where it was, joined by a torn-paper arrow entering low.
The arrow lifts, splitting into two paths beside the building.
A paper hand presses a black chip over the split, closing where we began.
beats.delivery: Micro-cap valuation prices in execution uncertainty, and upside is asymmetric.
